questions.mc_rejected_reason: The purpose is a single nuanced behavioral principle, not a factual name/actor/term with natural mutually-exclusive alternatives; any 4-option MC would either give the answer away through obviously-wrong distractors or produce distractors too close to fairly grade.
questions.text: What is this feature's core premise about how the quiet-hours window should be established?
questions.expected_answer: The window should be inferred from the user's actual observed notification-engagement behavior over time, rather than requiring the user to manually configure a fixed schedule.

questions.mc_rejected_reason: The distinction (sustained multi-day shift vs. single-day anomaly) is a comparative behavioral rule, not reducible to a small set of clean mutually-exclusive options without trivializing or muddying the comparison.
questions.text: Explain the difference in how the system responds to a sustained multi-day shift in engagement pattern versus a single anomalous day.
questions.expected_answer: A sustained shift across multiple consecutive days causes the inferred window to gradually move to reflect the new pattern, while a single anomalous day causes no shift at all — the system distinguishes durable pattern change from one-off noise.
questions.source_heading: FR-003; FR-004; User Story 2 Acceptance Scenarios

questions.text: A new user has just installed the app and has no behavioral history yet. According to this spec, what quiet-hours window should they be given, and why?
questions.expected_answer: A conservative default window, because there isn't yet sufficient behavioral history to support an inference; this avoids sending notifications at all hours for a brand-new user.

questions.text: Trace what happens if a user dismisses a notification that arrives during their currently-inferred quiet window. Is that interaction discarded, or does it affect future inference?
questions.expected_answer: It's treated as a valid signal like any other and feeds into the ongoing inference — it is not discarded as out-of-window noise.

questions.text: This spec requires both that the window never shifts on a single anomalous day (FR-004) and that it does shift gradually after a sustained change (FR-003). How would the system distinguish 'day 3 of a real shift' from 'just another anomalous day' before enough days have accumulated to be sure?
questions.expected_answer: The spec doesn't specify an exact day-count threshold — it establishes the behavioral contract (a single day never shifts it; multiple consecutive days does) without prescribing the underlying inference mechanism's precise boundary, leaving that as an implementation-level decision for planning rather than something spec.md itself resolves.
